page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-24 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 90.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is provided by an integrated NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU.

This instance type does not include local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. It also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external networking configurations for public internet access.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-24 offers a balanced allocation of dedicated compute cores and system memory alongside professional-grade GPU acceleration, making it a viable option for workloads that require GPU rendering without the extreme cost of enterprise-grade deep learning accelerators. Suitable workloads include 3D rendering, computer-aided design, video encoding, and moderately demanding graphics-intensive applications.
